Ling 285
Human Language and Computation
            Lecture 1


                          Khalil Iskarous
               Department of Linguistics
              University of Southern California

Speech and Language

• You learn to move your speech organs in
  extremely complex way with neither instructions,
  nor hardly any visual feedback.
• By 2-4 you can speak with a wide vocabulary and
  near-adult language, with hardly any explicit
  instruction.
• You may have also memorized the visual shape
  of the alphabet, but reading and writing whole
 wordscomes at 6-7, and requires a great deal of
  instruction.
• Articulatory Phonetics is the field that studies the
 movements of different vocal tract structures.
• And the last two year Voice Assistants and other
 Speech Tech have come to emulate the speech
  ability in ways none of us thought possible.
• Ling 285 is about Human and AI speech

Now think of the air between the tongue and the rest of the vocal
tract. And ignore the fact that it is curved. This is how air vibrates in
your vocal tract, schematically. That’s the subject matter of Acoustic
Phonetics.

AI: Ughhhhhh… Can’t we just ignore
AI?
• Given all we know about the psychological, economic, social, and
 environmental harm, can we just ignore AI– just pretend it doesn’t
  exist?
• Given the existential harm that many scientists warn about, can we just
 pretend it doesn’t exist?
• It exists, with many harms, and some benefits (e.g., immunotherapy,
 and yes, environmental engineering)
• One of the biggest dangers: We have no idea how it works. We know
  everything, and Understand nothing.
• And the people who know how it operates are very very few.
• In my opinion, AI literacy is necessary for scientists who use it,
  politicians who need to control it, lawyers who litigate on it, etc.
• I teach this course, because I believe that someone in a class like this, a
  creatve thinker can help us understand these systems enough to
  benefit from them, while avoiding their negative consequences

Goals of Ling 285

• Specific:
     • To appreciate the human cognitive skill of speech
     • To understand some basic principles of physics through speech
     • To understand how modern AI systems model human cognition
     • To sharpen your methodical reasoning via elementary programming
• General:
     • How to think creatively in a rich interdisciplinary way, as this course will
     involve physics, psychology, linguistics, biology, economics, computer
     science, philosophy, neuroscience, and many other fields.
     • To deepen your understanding of the world we are all living in today
     • To sharpen your skillful use of modern AI systems
